body:
Esjeje1 wrote:
> 
> Nick Halloway wrote:
> 
> >Society has been collapsing for a long time, hasn't it?  Apparently
> >it's always collapsing but always regenerating in other ways.  How
> >are the problems we have now different from the problems humanity has had for
> >thousands of years?
> >
> Good question.
> 
> It's probably more of a question of degree. There is no doubt that problems
> existed in other ages. But we now have the means to monitor human activity to
> an extremely minute degree. Much greater than ever before. Furthurmore, other
> types of societies have been forced to march in step, leaving few places where
> trulely independent souls can seek refuge. This is quite different than what
> was possible in the past, and adds a new dimension.
> 
> Finally, in view of the environmental havoc created by our society, it's
> doubtless high time for society to regenerate once again, before mother nature
> takes care of all our problems.
> 
> SJJ
> "Whoso wants to be a man must also be a non-conformist!" - Emerson
